newsitem.title: UK: EIB'S ESCUDO 1ST NON-CORE EMU BOND WITH EURO OPTION.
newsitem.headline: EIB'S ESCUDO 1ST NON-CORE EMU BOND WITH EURO OPTION.

text.p: The European Investment Bank on Thursday issued an escudo bond which may be redenominated in euros, the first such deal in a currency not widely expected to be part of the single European currency in January 1999.
Portuguese Banco CISF arranged the EIB's 20 billion escudo 10-year deal which may be redenominated in euros if or when Portugal adopts the euro.

Previous deals with redenomination clauses have been only in the three currencies widely regarded as being core to European economic and monetary union -- guilder, French franc and mark. The escudo financing will pay annual interest of 5.75 percent and be repaid on February 15, 2007.
These terms exactly match those on two outstanding EIB issues -- for 1.0 billion guilders and 3.0 billion French francs -- issued earlier this year.
If more than one of the three issues are redenominated in euros after EMU then they can be merged together to form a bigger, more easily tradeable bond. -- Dan Lalor, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8863
